title: How We Test an Autonomous Agent by Killing It
hook: Kill the agent mid-action, restart it, and check whether it lied about what happened.
thesis: The autonomous runtime specification already calls for killing execution at precise points: after decision, after durable-intent persistence, after claim, during external request, after external success before response, after response before verification, after verification before canonical recording, then restart. The episode shows one kill point end to end and asks the only question that matters: can an autonomous system recover without lying about what happened. Recovery that rewrites history is a failure; recovery that reports UNKNOWN and reconciles is the pass.

proven: The directive lists the kill points and the recovery-without-lying question (section 6).
The directive states uncertain effects must reconcile instead of being blindly repeated (section 6).
partial: That failure injection runs exist and are exercised, not only specified.
unknown: Recorded kill-and-restart runs with inspectable journal evidence suitable for publication.
